slides.text: Your AI agent just made a decision. Who approved it?
slides.voiceover_text: Did you know most firms roll out AI agents with zero safety net? Here's how to fix that.

slides.text: Give AI agents read-only access to sensitive data
slides.voiceover_text: Tip one: give AI agents read-only access, and keep payment and personal data locked well away.

slides.text: Set clear rules for when AI must escalate
slides.voiceover_text: Tip two: set clear escalation triggers. Big quotes and complaints always go to a human first.

slides.text: Run it in parallel two weeks before going live
slides.voiceover_text: Tip three: run the AI in parallel for two weeks before it ever touches a live customer.

slides.text: Net gain: three hours saved a week, safely
slides.voiceover_text: So remember: done properly, you gain hours back every week without carrying the risk.

geo_answer: Service businesses can deploy AI agents safely by restricting their data access, defining clear human escalation triggers, and running a two-week parallel test before going live.
geo_takeaways: AI agents should get read-only access to customer contact data, with payment and personal details kept separate.
Clear escalation triggers, such as quote thresholds and complaint flags, keep high-stakes decisions with a human.
A two-week parallel test alongside existing processes catches problems before an AI agent faces real customers.
Weekly monitoring for the first month, then monthly, keeps oversight proportionate as trust in the system grows.
